skirmish.label: Skirmish
descriptors: There's a fight ahead. Mind how close you let them get.
The scout recommends leaving room to step back after the first clash.
The scout marked where each foe stands. Check their reach before you close.

formation.label: Formation
descriptors: There are several jobs in that crew. Find the one the others depend on.
The scout marked who stands beside whom, not just how many there are.
Pick your first target carefully. What one foe does changes what the others can do.

ambush.label: Ambush
descriptors: The scout warns that you might not stay where you start.
Watch where the heavier threat could end up, not just where it stands now.
The scout drew arrows between positions rather than marking a front line.

rival_band.label: Rival band
descriptors: A rival band is on the road. The scout says they don't all fight alike.
The scout's notes read like a rival roster: less about how many, more about what each can do.
Watch how that band fights together. The one who rushes you first may not be the one to worry about.

telegraphed_strike.label: Heavy windup
descriptors: The scout saw a Bruiser prepare a heavy blow before striking the same spot.
Watch the ground where the Bruiser winds up. There is time to move before the blow lands.

ferryman_escort.label: Ferryman escort
descriptors: The ferryman is still on this bank. His ferry is on the other.
The crossing is blocked, and the passenger in need of an escort is the ferryman himself.

troll_eviction.label: Peaceful eviction
descriptors: The villagers want the troll out of their square, not dead in it.
Someone needs to lead the troll out of the square. The villagers were quite firm about keeping it alive.

pressure_gate.label: Pressure gate
descriptors: The gate lifts only while a living character stands on the plate.
The scout found a gate that opens for whoever stands on the plate, friend or foe.

holdout.label: Holdout
descriptors: Attackers are coming from both sides. Help is on its way, but not yet.
The line needs someone alive when relief arrives. It doesn't need an empty battlefield.

sheep_herding.label: Sheep herding
descriptors: Three sheep are loose, and they move away from anyone who gets too close.
The east pen is ready. The flock is not, and following right behind a sheep works better than greeting it head-on.

collapsing_bridge.label: Collapsing crossing
descriptors: The bridge is losing its spans in stages. The scout marked which go first.
The far bank is still reachable, but the planks won't wait for everyone.

quiet_retrieval.label: Quiet retrieval
descriptors: There's treasure ahead, and a giant asleep close enough to hear you.
The scout whispered this one: take the treasure, leave the giant sleeping.

ritual_circles.label: Ritual circles
descriptors: Three circles need occupants. The marks don't care whose side they're on.
The ritual needs all its circles occupied at the same time, and one round won't do.

wagon_defense.label: Wagon defense
descriptors: The supply wagon can't make headway with raiders beside it.
The road leads to the village, but the scout saw raiders bearing down on the wagon.
Three Harpooners wait across the road. Each can hit from two tiles away, so check their reach before stepping between them.
These three harpoons wound but don't pull. Stay more than two tiles from the raiders, or close on one without stepping into another's reach.
Five goblins are closing from both sides. They hit harder when two get beside the same target.
The goblins are weak on their own. Watch the gaps a second goblin could use to join the first.
A Hookhand and a Harpooner cover the lane. The Bruiser is already close enough to make a bad pull hurt.
The Hookhand can drag a hero within reach of the slower Bruiser. Look at where the hero would land, not just where they stand.
Two Shieldbearers flank an Archer. Each one beside the Archer cuts the damage the Archer takes.
The Archer is the threat at range. Separate each Shieldbearer from the Archer to break that protection.
The Captain tries to back away when heroes get beside him, but the three Grunts hit harder at his side.
The Grunts aren't stronger everywhere. It's standing next to the Captain that puts extra force behind their blows.
Two Bombers go off when they fall. A blast hits anyone next to the Bomber, even its own allies.
Watch the Harpooner's two-tile reach when picking a spot clear of the blast. The Bombers can set each other off while they're side by side.
Two Bruisers have a Healer who can repeatedly restore 3 HP to a wounded ally within two tiles.
The enemy Healer can heal without a cast limit, restoring 3 HP to a wounded ally within two tiles. A Bruiser out of reach gets no healing.
Two Duelists are waiting. A Duelist who survives a hit can strike back if the attacker is still beside them.
These two punish a clean hit at arm's length. Attack from farther away or leave a gap before the return blow.
The Trickster can trade places with the Ogre once. Watch for it to move closer to your company than the Ogre is.
The Ogre hits hard up close. A gap that looks safe from the Ogre may not be safe from a swap.
They brought a Knight who pushes, a Wizard who blasts the nearest character, and a Healer who patches up wounded allies.
The rival Healer can repeatedly restore 2 HP to wounded allies within two tiles. Their Wizard can hit their own side, and their Knight answers a taunt.
When a Bandit falls, the Fierce one hits harder and the Swift one moves farther. Those gains stack.
The Guard Bandit shrugs off part of a heavy hit once another Bandit is down. Small hits still get through, and the armor only improves once.
A Hookhand and a Harpooner cover the lane. The Hookhand can pull a hero closer while the Harpooner strikes from a distance.
Watch where the Hookhand's pull will land your hero, and check the Harpooner's reach before closing.
Tougher Shieldbearers flank the Archer. Each guard beside the Archer reduces the damage it takes.
These Shieldbearers take more punishment than the usual wall. Separate them from the Archer or work through their defenses.
These Bombers can survive hits that would fell the usual pair. Their death blasts hurt anyone beside them, including their allies.
The sturdier Bombers may need another hit before they explode. Watch the Harpooner's reach while choosing where to finish them.
The rival Wizard is tougher than usual and blasts the nearest character, friend or foe. A Knight and Healer fight alongside them.
Expect the sturdier rival Wizard to stay in the fight longer. The rival Healer can also patch up wounded allies.
A tougher enemy Healer supports two Bruisers and can repeatedly restore 3 HP to a wounded ally within 2 tiles.
The sturdier Healer can patch up wounded allies within two tiles. Separate a Bruiser from that support or focus on the Healer.
This Ogre is tougher than usual and hits hard up close. The Trickster can swap places with it once.
A sturdier Ogre may stay dangerous longer, and the Trickster can bring it closer with a single swap.
Two Hookhands can pull heroes toward the Bomber, which can strike up close before it falls. Its death blast hurts everyone beside it, friend or foe.
Two Harpooners strike from two tiles away while the Bomber closes in. Check both Hookhands' pulls and the Bomber's blast before committing.
Defeat the whole crew. Two Hookhands pull from separate approaches, with two Harpooners and a Bomber nearby. The Bomber's death blast hurts everyone beside it, friend or foe.
Defeat the Bruiser and Archer. A crate blocks the Archer's straight shot and the direct approach to the Bruiser; break it for a shortcut or keep the cover.
Defeat the Longbow and its Bruiser bodyguard. The Longbow needs a clear straight lane and cannot shoot an adjacent target, but the bodyguard is advancing.
Defeat both twins. The Fresh Twin hits harder at full health; the Wounded Twin hits harder once hurt. Consider whom you can finish before the return blow.
Defeat the Mercenary and Archer. The Mercenary pursues whoever last damaged him, even his own crew; without a living last attacker, he seeks heroes.
Defeat the Giant and his crew. The Giant sweeps everyone next to him, including his ally; keep clear or lure him into swinging beside the crew.
Defeat the Friar and his crew. When the Friar falls, he heals surviving enemies for 2 HP; finish him before spreading damage or save him for last.
Defeat the whole enemy crew. The first enemy corpse marks the bell's one attempt to raise a soldier at that tile, at the end of the following round. Block the tile or defeat everyone first.
Defeat the two Spearmen and their crew. Each adjacent strike continues one tile straight beyond its target, hitting anyone there, including an ally.
Defeat the two Spearmen and their crew. Their adjacent strikes continue one tile straight beyond the target, hitting anyone there, even their own crew. Watch both approaches.

Defeat the Bruiser and his crew. The Bruiser marks an adjacent opponent's tile, then smashes that tile for 6 damage on his next turn when he can act, even if an ally stands there. A skipped turn delays the blow; move away or defeat him first.

Defeat the Bruiser and two crew. The Bruiser marks an adjacent opponent's tile, then smashes it for 6 damage on his next turn when he can act, even if an ally stands there. A skipped turn delays the blow; move away or defeat him first.

Defeat two Bruisers and their crew. Each Bruiser marks an adjacent opponent's tile, then smashes it for 6 damage on his next turn when he can act, even if an ally stands there. A skipped turn delays his blow; move away or defeat him first.

Defeat two Bruisers and two crew. Each Bruiser marks an adjacent opponent's tile, then smashes it for 6 damage on his next turn when he can act, even if an ally stands there. A skipped turn delays his blow; move away or defeat him first.
Defeat the Lender, Bruiser and Archer. At each round's start the Lender protects the nearest other ally from its first damaging hit while the Lender lives; the Lender remains exposed.

Defeat the Lender, Bruiser and Archer. All three are tougher than usual. At each round's start the Lender protects the nearest other ally from its first damaging hit while the Lender lives; the Lender remains exposed.
A crate sits in the ferryman's path to the narrow bridge. A Harpooner waits across the gap.
Get the ferryman to the far bank by the end of round ten. Clearing the Harpooner alone won't get him to the ferry.
destination_descriptors: The last ferryman is stranded on the wrong bank. Get him to his ferry before the crossing gives way.
The ferryman can't get past a crate and a Harpooner on his own. Bring him across alive.

descriptors: The troll follows the nearest living hero and stops beside them. Draw it out of the marked square.
A shove will do if the troll ends the round outside the square. It has to survive the round.
destination_descriptors: A troll has taken over the village square. The villagers want the square back and the troll in one piece.
The village has asked for someone to show a stubborn guest the way out. Lead or shove the troll out alive.

descriptors: The plate at C2 opens the gate at D3 while any living character stands on it. Send a hero through to F3.
A goblin waits beyond the gate. The plate works under a goblin too, and the gate closes as soon as the plate is empty.
destination_descriptors: There's no key for this gate. Hold down the pressure plate long enough to get a hero to the far exit.
A goblin is watching the only way through. Put a living body on the plate and get one of your own out the far side.

descriptors: Goblins close in from both sides with a Bruiser to the east. Keep one hero alive through round six, when help arrives.
From round four, an Archer and a War Drummer join the attack when their entry tiles are clear. You don't need to defeat them to hold the line.
destination_descriptors: Relief is six rounds away and the line is under attack from both sides. Keep someone standing until help arrives.
The attackers have an Archer and a War Drummer in reserve. Hold long enough for your own relief to arrive.

descriptors: All three sheep need to reach the east pen alive. At round's end, loose sheep react to the nearest non-sheep within two tiles.
A sheep that can't get farther from whoever startled it may step toward the pen instead. Once penned, it settles.
destination_descriptors: Three sheep have bolted. Get the whole flock back into the east pen without losing one.
The shepherd is scattering the flock too. Put your heroes where the sheep will run toward the pen, not away from it.

descriptors: The C span drops at the end of round four and the E span at the end of round six. Don't be standing on either when it goes.
Get a living hero to G3 by the end of round eight. You can leave the raider behind; reaching the bank is what matters.
destination_descriptors: The bridge is coming down in sections. Get a hero to the far bank before the last of it goes.
A raider is on the failing bridge. You don't have to win that fight; you have to get across.

descriptors: The treasure is at E3. Each hero move adds one noise, another ability adds two, and a performance adds three.
Holding is silent. Even if a hero reaches the treasure early, the round has to end at twelve noise or less.
destination_descriptors: The treasure is within reach of a light-footed hero. Get to it without waking the giant.
A goblin is near the treasure and a giant is asleep. Take what you came for without making a full fight of it.

descriptors: All three circles must have living occupants at the end of two rounds in a row. Enemies and summons count.
A Hookhand can spoil your placement. One empty circle at round's end resets the count.
destination_descriptors: Three ritual circles need living occupants. Keep all three filled at the close of two rounds running.
The circles make no distinction between friend and foe. Use whoever is on hand to finish the ritual.

descriptors: Two raiders are coming for the wagon. A living enemy next to it stops it from moving that round.
Keep the route clear and the wagon can take one step at round's end. It has to reach the village intact.
destination_descriptors: The village is waiting on its last supply wagon. See it safely down the road while raiders close in.
Raiders are after the supplies. Keep them away from the wagon so it can reach the village under its own power.
